goal: Makes wallet transaction rebroadcasts use the private broadcast method when -privatebroadcast is enabled, instead of always broadcasting to all peers.
Closes a privacy gap where automatic rebroadcasts of wallet transactions leak sender IP information even when private broadcast is turned on.
reviewability: Paused. A substantive correctness concern about dependent (CPFP) transactions getting stuck under private broadcast rebroadcast is unresolved and the author has been silent since April.
Also needs rebase; conflicts with several open PRs touching the same wallet/logging code.
agreement: Concept ACKed by multiple reviewers (pablomartin4btc, w0xlt, andrewtoth) and two ACKs on a specific commit.

achow101 raised a concrete unresolved harm: private broadcast can strand CPFP-dependent child transactions for up to 24 hours or indefinitely, and the author only sketched possible fixes without implementing one.
instagibbs later confirmed the fix is only possible up to current 1P1C package relay limits, leaving the concern open.

result.summary: This PR changes the wallet's periodic transaction rebroadcast logic so that, when -privatebroadcast is enabled, rebroadcasts of wallet-related transactions use the private broadcast method rather than the default send-to-all broadcast. It also tweaks a wallet log message to print both txid and wtxid plus the submission outcome. It is a follow-up to the private broadcast feature introduced in #29415.
result.problem: Users who enable private broadcast to avoid leaking their IP when submitting transactions still had their wallet's automatic rebroadcasts sent via the ordinary send-to-all method, undermining the privacy benefit they opted into. This affects privacy-conscious wallet users and is discussed against the broader IP-leak issue #3828.

open_concerns: achow101: private broadcast rebroadcasting can strand dependent (CPFP) transactions because each transaction is privately sent to a different random peer, so a child transaction's parent may not be in the peer's mempool, delaying or indefinitely blocking rebroadcast; no implemented fix yet, only proposed approaches.

w0xlt: switching -privatebroadcast off/on across restarts could unexpectedly change how a given transaction was originally broadcast, since there is no per-tx tracking of broadcast method; author disagrees this is a problem.
mzumsande: the underlying IP-leak threat model concern (#3828) isn't fully addressed for IsMine() transactions on clearnet-only nodes.
sedited asked whether the PR should stay in draft while related work (#34707, package broadcast) is ongoing; unanswered.
resolved_concerns: w0xlt's initial characterization of this as merely a short-term pragmatic fix was pushed back on by the author, who considers it integral wallet support work, without further objection from w0xlt.
discussion.author_status: silent since 2026-04-28 (141 days), last force-push/rebase on that date; reviewer comments as recent as 2026-05-11 unanswered

result.card: This PR makes the wallet's periodic rebroadcast of unconfirmed wallet transactions use the private broadcast method (instead of send-to-all) when -privatebroadcast is enabled, closing a privacy gap left by #29415 where automatic rebroadcasts still leaked sender info. Several reviewers gave concept/commit ACKs (pablomartin4btc, w0xlt, andrewtoth), but achow101 raised a substantive unresolved concern that private broadcast rebroadcasting can strand CPFP-dependent child transactions for up to 24 hours or longer, since parent and child may be sent to different random peers; instagibbs later confirmed the fix is limited by current 1P1C package relay support. The author proposed possible fixes but has not implemented one, and has been silent since 2026-04-28, leaving the PR paused on a material open question and also needing a rebase due to conflicts with several other open PRs. Priority is moderate: a real but non-urgent privacy improvement for wallet users, tangential to core p2p broadcast mechanics themselves.
